title: Perspectives and influencing factors from the point of view of patients and relatives on dementia diagnostics in a general practitioner and specialist setting
summary: Around 1.8 million people in Germany live with dementia and the number is rising rapidly. A diagnosis is often made late and mainly in specialist centers. Possible reasons for this include fear of stigmatization and a lack of knowledge about possible points of contact. General practitioners are usually the first point of contact for symptoms of dementia, as there is often a relationship of trust and low-threshold access is possible. In a cooperation project at Witten/Herdecke University, optimized case-finding for dementia was investigated using tablet-based tests. Following digital testing, patients with abnormal test results indicating mild to severe cognitive impairment were referred to a memory outpatient clinic. A diagnosis of dementia (or its exclusion and a further differential diagnosis) was made there. Almost 300 study participants took advantage of this initial diagnosis option, but only a fraction of patients with conspicuous test results took up the offer of more detailed clarification at the specialist center. The reasons for this could only be ascertained informally in the project. An initial literature search revealed a large number of specialist articles on the timely diagnosis of dementia, but no systematic review or summary. Particularly not if patients have overcome the first hurdle of diagnosis in the GP setting, but reject further diagnosis. The aim of the project is therefore to qualitatively survey patients and their relatives on subjectively perceived and/or experienced facilitating and hindering factors after initial diagnosis in the GP setting and to bring them together with the current state of the international literature through a scoping review on barriers and facilitating factors in dementia diagnosis in order to contribute to an improved approach in dementia diagnosis and thus positively influence care for all those involved.

interventions.name: 7-10 qualitative individual interviews each with patients and relatives are planned in the 2nd and 3rd quarter of 2025
Single focus group with a Patient Advisory Board of the Universität Witten/Herdecke in the 1st quarter of 2026
Conduction of a scoping review on enabling and hindering factors for timely dementia diagnosis in the 2nd quarter of 2026

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
sufficient knowledge of German; sufficient cognitive status of the patients to understand the contents of the study and to be able to give their consent
Exclusion criteria:
Persons under the age of 18, with insufficient knowledge of German and
a cognitive status that no longer permits informed consent to the study.
